official.deadline_note: AY 2026-27 round closed; A2A portal was open from 27 February 2026 with 15 April 2026 as the last date for submission of applications (High Commission of India, Kuala Lumpur notice of 6 March 2026). ICCR allocates QUAD slots only for AY 2025-26 to AY 2027-28.
official.application_cycle: AY 2026-27 (round closed); scheme offered for AY 2025-26 to AY 2027-28
official.status_note: The AY 2026-27 application round closed on 15 April 2026; ICCR's scheme-wise allocation lists 50 QUAD slots funded by MEA, offered only for AY 2025-26 to 2027-28.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official scheme table lists facilities as 'Stipend, HRA, Contingent Allowances, Thesis/Dissertation Allowance, Airfare, Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)'.
benefits: Stipend, HRA, Contingent Allowances, Thesis/Dissertation Allowance, Airfare, Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)
Monthly stipend INR 18,000 for Undergraduate students, payable from the date of joining the institute
Monthly House Rent Allowance INR 6,500 in Grade I cities and INR 5,500 in other cities, paid along with the monthly stipend
Annual contingent allowance INR 5,000 for Undergraduate students
One-time thesis/dissertation allowance INR 7,000 for UG (only where a project report is a course requirement)
Return economy class airfare to the airport nearest to the place of study and 3-tier AC train fare to the place of study in India, if so required
eligibility: Open to students from the Indo-Pacific region only: 32 country/mission entries with fixed slot allocations (e.g. Bangladesh 3, Kenya 3, Myanmar 3, Madagascar 5, Seychelles 5); total 50 slots

Undergraduate level only, in B.Tech courses at the 8 designated institutes: MNIT Jaipur, NIT Durgapur, NIT Tiruchirappalli, Delhi Technological University, NIT Warangal, CUSAT Kochi, Anna University Chennai, IIIT Delhi
For BE/B.Tech courses, Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics are compulsory in grades 11 and 12
Age 18 to 35 years for undergraduate courses (undergraduate age 18 years as on 1 July 2026, per the AY 2026-27 ICCR mission notice)
Medical, law and integrated courses are prohibited under the scheme
requirements: Apply online through the A2A ICCR Scholarship Portal; only online applications are accepted, and no changes are possible after final submission
A 500-word essay in English to ascertain English proficiency; TOEFL/IELTS or other standardised test scores may additionally be submitted if available
Certified English translations of all documents whose originals are not in English; applications without them are not considered
Medical fitness certificate duly filled by a medical practitioner in the format prescribed by ICCR, submitted to the Mission and uploaded on the A2A portal
Compulsory medical insurance policy with a minimum sum assured of INR 5,00,000 (five lakh) per annum, procured by the student at own expense, before travel or immediately after reaching India
If stipulated by the university/institute in the offer letter, an Association of Indian Universities (AIU) equivalence certificate, obtained at the student's own non-reimbursable expense
documents: Mark sheets and transcripts in English for grade 10 and grade 10+2 (or equivalent) with certified translations where originals are not in English
Birth certificate and school leaving certificate
Nationality certificate and identity card provided by the applicant's government
Medical fitness certificate in the ICCR-prescribed format
Medical insurance policy evidence with minimum cover of INR 5,00,000 per annum
AIU equivalence certificate, where the allotted university/institute stipulates it
selection_criteria: Selection for the scholarship award is done independently by the Indian Missions/Posts abroad on the basis of merit
Admission is decided by the concerned university/institute on the applicant's credentials and its own eligibility criteria; ICCR and the Mission have no role in the admission decision
Universities/institutes may conduct an online interview of applicants if required

Applicants may list up to 5 universities/institutes in order of preference; admission is given as far as possible per preference, but candidates may be offered a lower preference where preferred institutes are oversubscribed
coverage: Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)
Monthly stipend (UG INR 18,000), House Rent Allowance (INR 6,500 Grade I cities / INR 5,500 other cities) and annual contingent allowance (UG INR 5,000)
Return economy class airfare to the airport nearest to the place of study and 3-tier AC train fare if so required

Charges payable by the student: hostel/private accommodation charges, mess charges, security deposit, caution money, fees for obtaining all certificates, registration fees/penalties for registration/updation with immigration authorities, and any other fees/charges not covered under scholarship norms
Expenditure on laboratory chemicals and other related incidental charges for science courses is borne by the scholars themselves
application_method: Register with a unique User ID and password on the A2A ICCR Scholarship Portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in)
Complete the online application, save each page, and submit before the deadline; submit through the Indian Embassy/Mission in the applicant's own country
List up to 5 universities/institutes in order of preference and attach the 500-word English essay and all certificates/transcripts with English translations
official.application_route: Apply online on the A2A ICCR Scholarship Portal and submit the application through the Indian Embassy/High Commission in the applicant's own country; the Mission awards the scholarship after the university confirms provisional admission.
official.citizenship_residency: Only nationals of the listed Indo-Pacific countries/missions with allocated slots may apply, and applications must be submitted through the Indian Mission in the applicant's own country
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is exclusively for international students from the 32 listed Indo-Pacific country/mission entries (50 slots total); it is not open to Indian nationals
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: STEM/Engineering only (B.Tech) at the 8 designated Government of India-funded technical institutions, administered by ICCR (AMS Division) on behalf of the Ministry of External Affairs, with fixed country-wise slot allocations
official.description: Announced at the Quad Leaders' Summit 2024 held in Wilmington, Delaware, USA, the QUAD STEM Scholarship Scheme awards fifty scholarships to students from the Indo-Pacific region to pursue a 4-year Undergraduate Engineering (B.Tech) programme at Government of India-funded technical institutions. ICCR launched the scheme for the Indo-Pacific countries for AY 2025-26 and continues to offer it through AY 2027-28, with 50 slots funded by the Ministry of External Affairs.
official.region: Indo-Pacific (32 country/mission entries, Asia-Pacific and Indian Ocean region)
official.english_requirement: No fixed IELTS/TOEFL score is prescribed: a 500-word essay in English is required to ascertain English proficiency, TOEFL/IELTS scores may optionally be submitted, the medium of instruction is English, and universities may interview applicants online

not_confirmed: QUAD-specific deadline and timeline for the next cycle after AY 2026-27 (only the AY 2025-26 and AY 2026-27 timelines are published)
Any QUAD-specific variation from the published programme-wide financial norms (the UG rates are taken from ICCR's own financial terms, applied to the B.Tech level)
verification.notes: Amounts and coverage taken from ICCR's own published Financial Terms (as of July 2021) and Policy_Guidelines.pdf on the A2A portal; scheme mechanics, slots, institutes and AY 2026-27 deadline (15 April 2026) from ICCR's own scheme pages and official Indian Mission publications of the ICCR notice.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50-seat, government-funded full B.Tech ride at one of eight named Indian engineering institutions, but only if you hold a passport from one of the 32 listed Indo-Pacific countries or missions - Bangladesh, for example, has just 3 seats. The money is concrete: INR 18,000 per month stipend, INR 5,500-6,500 monthly house rent, INR 5,000 annual contingency, tuition paid straight to the institute, and a return economy airfare. Budget for what is not covered: hostel/mess bills, a mandatory INR 5-lakh medical insurance you buy yourself, AIU equivalence fees, and lab incidentals.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recent 12th-grade leaver (18-35) with strong Physics-Chemistry-Mathematics marks from an Indo-Pacific country where your Indian Mission holds at least one QUAD seat.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country's exact slot count on the ICCR scheme page and open a dialogue with your Indian Mission's education wing before the portal opens
Scan grade 10 and 10+2 mark sheets early and get certified English translations ready - untranslated documents are rejected outright
Draft the 500-word English essay and, if you have one, attach TOEFL/IELTS scores
Book the ICCR-format medical fitness check and arrange the INR 5-lakh medical insurance policy before travel
Shortlist courses at the 8 eligible institutes and check each university's own prerequisites before listing your 5 preferences
Submit on the A2A portal well before the mid-April deadline; the form cannot be edited after submission
common_rejection_risks: Applying for an institution or course outside the 8 designated B.Tech programmes - everything else is ineligible
Missing Physics, Chemistry or Mathematics in grades 11-12, which is a hard requirement for engineering
Incomplete applications or missing English translations, which universities summarily reject
Being outside the 18-35 age band for undergraduate on the stated reference date
Assuming a scholarship offer guarantees admission - universities make their own admission decisions on your credentials
Expecting to switch course or university later: a change request at admission can void the offer, and mid-way withdrawal triggers full repayment of ICCR's spend
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel or private accommodation rent and mess charges, security deposits and caution money, the mandatory INR 5-lakh-per-annum medical insurance premium bought by the student, AIU equivalence certificate fees (non-reimbursable), certificate/registration fees and immigration (FRRO) charges, laboratory chemicals and science incidental charges, and any initial living costs before the first stipend release - no cash is paid until the bank account is operational.
document_audit: Grade 10 AND 10+2 mark sheets both need English transcripts - uploading only the final year's is a classic failure
The ICCR fitness certificate must be in the exact prescribed format signed by a registered medical practitioner
AIU equivalence is only needed where the allotted institute stipulates it in its offer letter - check the offer before paying for it

Originals (mark sheets, birth certificate, school leaving certificate, nationality certificate, government ID, passport) must be carried in English and produced on arrival; a mismatch with portal data cancels the admission
A State Bank of India account must be opened within a month of arrival and arrival details reported on the Gyan Setu app within 15 days, or stipend payment stalls
alerts: The AY 2026-27 window closed on 15 April 2026; the scheme itself is authorised only for AY 2025-26 to 2027-28, so the next chance is the 2027-28 cycle (portal historically opens in late February)
Applications must go through your own country's Indian Mission - applying from a third country changes the submission route
Engineering students lose the scholarship if they fail their third or fourth year and cannot revive it by simply re-enrolling; clearing the backlog is required first
No part-time or full-time work is permitted while studying, and you must leave India once the provisional certificate is issued
Staying outside India beyond 30-60 days attracts pro-rata deductions on the stipend under ICCR's published rules
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the A2A portal, submit the online application with 5 university preferences, essay and documents before the deadline, then the university vets and provisionally admits, the Mission allocates the scholarship and issues the offer letter, and you accept, join via SII/FRRO visa processing and report arrival on Gyan Setu.
